Current production critical CDIs are degraded and approaching failure. There are insufficient replacement units available. 
 
400SW manufacturing relies on purified water for its operation, with the purified water stream reliant upon redundant RO trains (Train #1 and #2). These RO trains include CDI (continuous deionizing) units which are integral to the purification stream. If the CDIs on RO Train #1 (currently displaying unacceptable performance) fail completely, then mitigation to the PW stream impact would take the form of redundant RO Train #2. However, without the purchase of new replacement CDIs, this mitigation method would be considered temporary. Insufficient CDIs are available in inventory to replace the failed inline units on RO Train #1, so the failed CDIs would need to be sent out for refurbishment (if even eligible). This process takes 8-12 weeks, during which time there would be no remaining redundancy for the PW stream, putting the entirety of 400SW manufacturing at risk.
This project (material procurement) will improve the reliability of the impacted manufacturing support system (RO trains and purified water streams) and preserve required capacity.

Avoiding possible loss of manufacturing production at 400SW.  A number of  in-service CDIs are degrading in condition affecting Reverse Osmosis process parameters and our ability to reliably produce purified water for production. There are insufficient available assets to replace failing CDIs. Executing the CDI purchase will enable direct replacements to the in-service at risk assets and preserve ability to produce purified water for production.
Worn CDIs can force the system to compensate for the decreased efficiency and therefore generate excess heat. Overheating and excess heat can create safety hazards.
